name: utility-interconnection
description: How utility interconnection, pre-PTO backfeed/energization, witness tests and permission to operate normally work, the reviewer's two-layer check (procedural conditions, then an independent engineering review of the customer's records against the adopted code), walking the operating states, a typical electrical review list, and how a professional determination memo or customer letter is written. Use for any interconnection, energization, PTO, commissioning-approval or utility-reply task.
---

# Utility interconnection, energization and permission to operate (PTO)
Typical lifecycle: application -> screening / studies -> interconnection agreement (ISA) -> construction
(customer facilities under an electrical permit from the authority having jurisdiction, AHJ; utility facilities
under a work order paid by the customer) -> AHJ final inspection and approval -> utility commissioning (metering,
telemetry/RTU end-to-end test, POI protective device acceptance) -> witness test or documented waiver -> written
PTO. Parallel operation before PTO happens only for a witness test under a switching order.
Pre-PTO backfeed / energization for commissioning: utility energizes the customer's transformer and collection
system with the generators disabled and isolated (inverter disconnects open and locked). Normally requires: an
agreement term allowing it, a written request, AHJ final approval of the work being energized, customer
equipment complete and safe to energize (code-compliant wiring, grounding, overcurrent
protection, labels, disconnects), metering set, switching order.
Reviewer's duties:
- Two separate checks: (1) procedural conditions in the agreement, tariff, standards and permit; (2) an
  independent engineering review of the customer's construction records line by line against the code edition
  the permit adopts and the utility standards. Do this even when the AHJ has passed the work; an approval by
  another party is evidence, not proof. A code non-conformance in the record must be corrected and documented
  before energization/PTO.
- Walk the operating states: before PTO (POI device open), during the requested operation, normal parallel
  operation, after a POI trip or utility outage. In each state ask what is energized, what must remain in
  service, and what must be isolated.
- Functions that must keep working (telemetry and RTU, protection relays, communications, remote control, metering):
  trace each one's power supply back to its source (station service, auxiliary transformer, battery/UPS and its
  autonomy) and check it stays energized in every operating state, including while the POI device is open; a
  confirmation obtained in one operating state does not prove another.
- Equipment that will be energized must comply as installed, whatever the generators are doing: generation being
  disabled does not excuse wiring-method, support, labelling, rating or protection defects in the energized part.
- Every finding, adverse or favourable, opens and quotes the clause it relies on and checks its conditions and
  exceptions (a clause that permits the installation removes an apparent violation; a clause not read cannot support
  "compliant").
- Respect the stated scope; where an out-of-scope item depends on something in scope, review the in-scope part.
- Review electrical construction records by NEC article (the edition the permit adopts), plus the utility's
  interconnection standards: 110 (equipment ratings vs available fault current, working space, enclosure ratings,
  markings); 240 (overcurrent protection); 250 (grounding and bonding, equipment grounding and electrode conductors);
  300/310 (wiring methods for the location, support, burial, ampacity with correction factors and terminal ratings);
  312/314 (cabinets, boxes, enclosures); 690 (PV circuits, dc voltage, disconnects, rapid shutdown, labels); 705
  (interconnected sources: point of connection, busbar and conductor rules, disconnects); 706 (energy storage).
Professional reply / memo:
- First sentence answers the question one way or the other (yes / no / not on that date) with the decisive reason.
- For each obstacle: what it is, the exact requirement (document, clause, edition), the evidence in the record,
  what must be done, by whom (name the customer when it is theirs), whether it can be done before the date, and
  what happens if not. Then the path to "yes" (what to resubmit, who re-inspects).
- Items checked and found acceptable: brief list.
- Internal memo vs external letter: an external letter does not cite internal directives or staff deliberations,
  stays short (1-2 pages), and gives one contact. An internal memo can cite internal procedures.
- Do not call a real obstacle a "confirmation", and do not raise an obstacle you have not verified.
- The tracker item (ticket / work package) mirrors the determination: one line per open item with owner and due date.
Before sending: re-check every cited clause and table value against the source; check dates and notice periods
with a script; check that the answer, the open items and the ticket agree; check names and titles against the
contact directory; check that nothing dated after the "as of" date was used.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE deliverable checker (runs inside the task container).

Re-opens each deliverable the way the recipient's software would and reports problems:
missing or empty files, unreadable archives, CSV/JSON/XLSX/DOCX/IFC that do not
parse, placeholder values (TBD, NaN, ...), Python that does not compile.
Standard library only; uses ifcopenshell when it is importable.

Generic by design: it knows file formats, never anything about a task. It does
not judge engineering correctness; that is what your own requirement checks are for.

Usage: python3 ahpele_check.py <file-or-dir> [<file-or-dir> ...] [--expect-columns a,b,c]
Exit code 0 when no problem was found, 1 otherwise.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
import os
import py_compile
import re
import sys
import zipfile
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET

PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"^\s*(TBD|TBA|TBC|to be (determined|advised|confirmed)|NaN|-?Inf(inity)?|XXX+|<fill[^>]*>|"
                         r"\?\?+|TODO|FIXME|placeholder|lorem ipsum)\s*$", re.I)
PLACEHOLDER_IN_TEXT = re.compile(r"\b(TBD|TBA|TODO|FIXME|XXX+|lorem ipsum)\b|<fill in>|\[insert[^\]]*\]", re.I)
problems: list[str] = []
notes: list[str] = []


def problem(msg):
    problems.append(msg)


def note(msg):
    notes.append(msg)


def check_csv(name, data):
    text = data.decode("utf-8-sig", "replace")
    try:
        rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))
    except csv.Error as exc:
        problem(f"{name}: CSV does not parse: {exc}")
        return
    if not rows:
        problem(f"{name}: CSV is empty")
        return
    header = [h.strip() for h in rows[0]]
    if len(set(h.lower() for h in header)) != len(header):
        problem(f"{name}: duplicate column names in header {header}")
    if any(not h for h in header):
        problem(f"{name}: empty column name in header")
    widths = {len(r) for r in rows[1:] if r}
    if widths and widths != {len(header)}:
        problem(f"{name}: rows have {sorted(widths)} cells but the header has {len(header)}")
    bad = [(i + 2, header[j] if j < len(header) else j, c) for i, r in enumerate(rows[1:]) for j, c in enumerate(r)
           if PLACEHOLDER.match(c or "")]
    if bad:
        problem(f"{name}: {len(bad)} placeholder cell(s), e.g. row {bad[0][0]} column {bad[0][1]!r} = {bad[0][2]!r}")
    note(f"{name}: CSV {len(rows) - 1} rows x {len(header)} columns: {', '.join(header[:30])}"
         f"{' ...' if len(header) > 30 else ''}")
    expect = os.environ.get("AHPELE_EXPECT_COLUMNS")
    if expect:
        norm = lambda s: re.sub(r"[\s_\-]+", "_", s.strip().lower())  # noqa: E731
        missing = [c for c in expect.split(",") if norm(c) not in {norm(h) for h in header}]
        if missing:
            problem(f"{name}: missing expected columns {missing}")

# Electrical safety, studies and acceptance (engineer's practice)
Project documents govern (spec, owner safety program, adopted NEC/NFPA 70E editions, utility data). Values below are
typical or from recent editions; re-read the actual table before quoting. Sizing and fault calcs: electrical-power-design.
## 1. Study basis and scenarios
- Model from field-verified data: utility max AND min fault MVA with X/R, transformers, cables, motors, generators,
  devices and settings as installed. Maximum case (all motors, ties closed) for equipment duty; minimum case (utility
  min, generator only, ties open): lower current can mean longer clearing and HIGHER incident energy; cover every mode
  (maintenance switch, tie, generator). Re-assess arc flash ≥ every 5 years and after changes (70E 130.5(G)).
## 2. Arc flash (IEEE 1584-2018, NFPA 70E)
- Range: 3φ 208 V-15 kV; I_bf 0.5-106 kA (≤ 600 V), 0.2-65 kA (601 V-15 kV); gap 6.35-76.2 mm LV, 19.05-254 mm MV;
  working distance ≥ 305 mm. Outside it (1φ, DC, > 15 kV) use another method (e.g. 70E Annex D for DC) and say so.
- Inputs per bus: V_oc, I_bf, electrode configuration (VCB, VCBB, HCB, VOA, HOA), gap, enclosure size, working distance,
  duration = clearing time of the device that actually clears a fault there (line side of a main -> upstream/primary
  device) at the ARCING current. Compute at I_arc and at reduced I_arc,min (variation factor); keep the worse energy.
- Typ. gap/working dist. (mm): 15 kV swgr 152/914; 5 kV swgr 104/914; LV swgr 32/610; LV MCC/panel 25/457; cable box 13/457.
- Outputs: I_arc, incident energy E (cal/cm²; 1 cal/cm² = 4.184 J/cm²), arc-flash boundary where E = 1.2 cal/cm²
  (5.0 J/cm²). E ≈ proportional to time; a 2 s cap only where egress is clearly possible (state it). 3φ ≤ 240 V with
  I_bf < 2 kA: sustained arc unlikely per 1584-2018 (label per owner policy).
- 70E PPE: incident energy method (arc rating ≥ E) or PPE category tables 130.7(C)(15)(a)/(b), valid only within their
  listed fault current and clearing time; categories 1 = 4, 2 = 8, 3 = 25, 4 = 40 cal/cm². Above 40: no category, plan
  de-energized work (electrically safe work condition 120.5: LOTO, test before touch); energized work permit 130.2(B).
- Shock approach (AC, Table 130.4(E)(a)): limited 3.0 m (10 ft) for movable conductors; fixed parts 1.0 m (3 ft 6 in)
  at 50-750 V, 1.5 m (5 ft) at 751 V-15 kV; restricted: avoid contact (50-150 V), 0.3 m (151-750 V), ≈ 0.7 m (0.75-15 kV).
- Label (70E 130.5(H), NEC 110.16): nominal voltage, arc-flash boundary, EITHER incident energy with working distance OR
  PPE category (not both), minimum arc rating/site PPE, and the date where the adopted code requires it.
- Mitigation: NEC 240.87 breakers ≥ 1200 A (ZSI, differential, maintenance switch, active mitigation, instantaneous below
  arcing current); 240.67 fuses ≥ 1200 A (≤ 0.07 s); current-limiting fuses, arc-flash relays, remote racking, HRG.
## 3. Protection coordination (IEEE 242, relay practice)
- TCC: log-log, currents on one voltage base (scale by turns ratio). Fuses: minimum melt to total clear band. Electronic
  trip: long-time pickup 0.4-1.0 × In + delay band, short-time 1.5-10 × Ir at 0.1-0.5 s (I²t in/out), instantaneous
  2-15 × In, ground fault (≤ 1200 A, ≤ 1 s at 3000 A where 230.95 applies).
- Margins: relay-relay CTI ≈ 0.3 s electromechanical, 0.2 s numeric; LV breakers/fuses: no band overlap, and in the
  instantaneous region only manufacturer selectivity tables prove selectivity; fuse-fuse by ratio tables.
- Phase 51 above maximum load incl. permitted overload (typ. 125-150 %) yet ≥ 1.5-2 × pickup at minimum fault; 51N/51G as
  low as unbalance allows; 50 above the maximum through-fault at the next bus and above transformer inrush.
- Transformer: primary device right of inrush (8-12 × FLC at 0.1 s), left of IEEE C57.109 through-fault curve; Δ-Y: a
  secondary L-G fault shows as 58 % on the primary (shift the curve). Cable damage (ICEA P-32-382): (I/A)²·t =
  0.0297·log10[(T2 + 234)/(T1 + 234)] Cu (A cmil, t s; Al 0.0125 and 228), XLPE 90 -> 250 °C. Motor: relay above
  starting curve, below hot stall time; 50 ≥ 1.6-2 × LRC. Deliver a settings table (CT ratio, pickups, curves) + TCCs.

§1  SCOPE
This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
equipped in a given deployment window.
This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.
Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
§12.2.
§2  COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.


--- page 2 ---
OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 2
Factor definitions:
•
Essential-service function. A site whose primary served load is a public water or wastewater facility;
a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
designation on the interconnection application.
•
Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
•
Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
verification, controls.
•
Queue date as tiebreaker. The interconnection queue date of the site's underlying application, used
only to break a tie among sites that rank equally on factors (1), (2), and (3).
External advocacy, correspondence volume, elected-official inquiries, and stakeholder communications
received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
evidenced by the source documents in §3.
§3  DOCUMENTATION
For each deployment window the DER Program Office shall assemble a deployment worksheet listing
every site meeting the eligibility conditions of §1, with the following fields drawn from the identified system
of record:
•
Site name and interconnection application ID (DER Program queue).
•
Customer / party of record and site service address (DER Program queue).
•
Nameplate capacity and program-scope classification per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (application file).
•
Devices required to energize (RTU, POI recloser, or both), quantities, and specification references
(Standards Engineering).
•
Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
•
Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
attached by reference (customer submission).
•
Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached by
reference (application file).
•
Interconnection queue date (DER Program queue).
The worksheet shall record the §2 factor on which each ranked site qualifies. Sites that do not qualify at
ranks (1) or (2) are ranked by (3) with (4) as tiebreaker. The worksheet, the ranked deployment list, and
the assigned equipment-set identifiers shall be retained in the DER Program equipment-planning file for
the applicable window and provided to the SOC concurrent with the coordination step described in §5.


--- page 3 ---
OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 3
Amendments to the worksheet arising after issuance — for example, receipt of previously missing
documentation for a listed site, or arrival of a new site into the waiting population — shall be recorded in an
addendum bearing its own date; prior ranked lists are not overwritten.
§4  VENDOR ENGAGEMENT EXPECTATIONS
Distribution Operations, working through Supply Chain, shall maintain rolling engagement with the current
approved suppliers of RTUs and POI reclosers with the following expectations:
•
Lead-time visibility. A monthly written statement of committed lead times, next scheduled delivery
date, and delivery quantity per device type, retained in the equipment-planning file. Any change to a
previously committed date or quantity is to be flagged in writing on receipt.
•
Order coverage. Standing purchase orders shall cover no fewer than the number of device sets
required to satisfy the sites eligible under §1 for the current deployment window plus the next
scheduled delivery window. Expedite requests shall be pursued where a delivery-date change would
displace a rank-(1) or rank-(2) site.
•
Alternate sourcing. Where committed lead times exceed the interval between deliveries, Supply
Chain shall document the shortcoming of the current approved suppliers and evaluate qualification of
additional vendors under Standards Engineering's certification procedures. Qualification effort shall
not condition or delay deployment decisions for the current window.
•
Substitution. Any proposed substitution of device model or configuration relative to the site's
approved specification is routed to Standards Engineering; substitutions are not accepted on
schedule pressure alone.
•
Escrow / spares. A minimum spare quantity per device type shall be held at the operations
warehouse, replenished on drawdown, and not consumed to accelerate a lower-ranked site ahead of
a higher-ranked site whose device set is en route.
Vendor engagement records are subject to audit by Regulatory Affairs on request.
§5  COORDINATION WITH THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS CENTER
The ranked deployment list issued under §3 is transmitted to the SOC concurrent with its issuance.
Coordination steps are as follows:
•
Pre-deployment briefing. For each device set scheduled to arrive in the deployment window, the
DER Program Office and the SOC Shift Supervisor confirm the receiving site, the anticipated
field-installation window, the commissioning sequence, and the telemetry integration steps required
for permission-to-operate (PTO). Nothing in this guideline modifies the SOC's PTO gating criteria;
TCS-02 §5 requires utility-owned RTU and SCADA telemetry with live telemetry established prior to
PTO for sites at or above 500 kW, and this guideline does not authorize interim or provisional
energization ahead of that condition.
•
Change control. A change to the ranked list after transmittal to the SOC — for example, arrival of a
new rank-(1) site, or documented lapse of a committed deadline previously credited at rank (2) — is
issued by written addendum jointly to Supply Chain and to the SOC. Verbal reprioritization is not to be
relied upon.
•
Field constraints. Where feeder condition, crew availability, or outage-window constraints prevent
installation at a higher-ranked site within the window, the SOC records the constraint and the DER
Program Office reissues the deployment assignment for that device set to the next-eligible site; the


--- page 4 ---
OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 4
higher-ranked site retains its rank for the following window.
•
Commissioning readiness. The SOC's PTO-hold log continues to govern which completed sites are
eligible for energization steps; sites without established telemetry remain on the hold log until the
utility-owned RTU is installed and telemetry is verified in accordance with TCS-02.
•
Reporting. A written record of device-set assignments, installation dates, commissioning outcomes,
and any addenda issued during the window is retained by the DER Program Office and made
available to Regulatory Affairs and to the SOC on request.
End of Guideline OG-17.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)

Re:  Pre-PTO backfeed request — Halbray Field Solar Site 3 (PXA-2024-0002), feeder ALN-159 — requested date July 29, 2025
Dear Ms. Strathe:
We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025. The gating item is the final electrical approval from Kelloway Township. Permit EP-25-0418 states that no permitted work shall be energized before final approval, and the final inspection is only booked for July 24, 2025; no final approval is in the record yet. If the Township passes the inspection and issues final approval on July 24, 2025, and the items below are closed, we can support energization on July 29, 2025. If final approval is not issued, we cannot energize on July 29, 2025; we will re-date the request with Distribution Operations.
Basis for this answer
The executed ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3 (11/18/2024) permits pre-PTO backfeed on your written request: the Company may energize the customer's facilities from the feeder for construction and commissioning power before PTO, provided the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel, with Distribution Operations performing the switching under its own switching order. Your July 9, 2025 letter is that written request, and it confirms the inverters will remain disabled.
The limit is the permit, not the ISA. Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 (issued 05/12/2025) adopts the 2023 NEC and states: “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval.” The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The backfeed would energize that work. Your letter and our commissioning checklist record the final inspection as booked for July 24, 2025; the permit itself records only that it is booked by the permit holder, and no final approval has been issued.
Record check on the customer-side equipment
What is already in order for the backfeed
Construction is reported complete on 07/03/2025, and the equipment schedules (Drawings E-201 and E-301, Rev B, 06/20/2025) record the four 575 kW skids, the 800 V collection system, switchboard CSB-1, transformer T-1 and the 13.2 kV primary switch.
The utility RTU is installed and its end-to-end point-to-point test was accepted by SCADA/EMS Engineering on 07/02/2025 (TCS-02 §3.6).
The POI recloser settings and protection coordination study were issued by Distribution Protection Engineering on 06/16/2025, and site acceptance items 1 to 7 were accepted in writing on 07/07/2025 (DPS-07 §5.1 and §6.2). Those items remain under that group's separate review; we have not re-reviewed them here.
Revenue meter RM-0002 was set by Alleniom Metering on 07/08/2025; Metering will confirm its final test and seal before switching.
The installed inverters, NG-XT-225 (eight) and NG-XT-125 (four), are in the body of the current CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025).
The witness test and the SOC's live-telemetry confirmation are conditions of PTO, not of the pre-PTO backfeed; they do not stand in the way of July 29.
What must be closed before July 29, 2025
Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. (the permit holder). Pass the final inspection on 07/24/2025 and send the written final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office as soon as it is issued, and in any event before the switching order is released. If the inspection is postponed, fails, or is not followed by written approval, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send us the isolation procedure and the signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed.
Two construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection — Tamsworth. These are confirmations, not additional utility requirements if the installed work already complies; they need to be in the record so they do not become a second gate at the final inspection:
(a)  CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. NEC 2023 110.16(B) requires those fields. The label should also carry the arc-flash boundary and either the incident energy at the working distance or the PPE category needed for the contractor's energized-work procedure. Confirm the installed label carries them, or replace it.
(b)  Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method.
Path to July 29, 2025
If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025, Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and will control the actual switching. If any item slips, we will not energize on July 29; we will give you the next available date after the item is closed.
Scope of this letter
This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed. The RTU and POI recloser acceptance, the recloser settings and protection coordination study, the backfeed switching, the queue position, and the system impact study and its conditions are being handled by their respective owners and are not re-reviewed here. The witness test and SOC live-telemetry confirmation remain PTO conditions.

What must be closed before July 29, 2025
1. Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors
   Inc. (the permit holder). Pass the final inspection on 07/24/2025 and send the written
   final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office as soon as it is issued, and in
   any event before the switching order is released. If the inspection is postponed, fails,
   or is not followed by written approval, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
2. Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock
   AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send us
   the isolation procedure and the signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the
   generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed.
3. Two construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection —
   Tamsworth. These are confirmations, not additional utility requirements if the
   installed work already complies; they need to be in the record so they do not become a
   second gate at the final inspection:
     (a) CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal
        voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. NEC
        2023 110.16(B) requires those fields. The label should also carry the arc-flash
        boundary and either the incident energy at the working distance or the PPE
        category needed for the contractor's energized-work procedure. Confirm the
        installed label carries them, or replace it.
     (b) Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in
        rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit
        single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from
        underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and
        marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method.
Path to July 29, 2025
If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025,
Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching
window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control the actual
switching. If any item slips, we will give you the next available date.
Scope of this letter
This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings,
coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue position, and the system
impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not re-reviewed here.

s.rennick@alleniom.com, copied to der.program@alleniom.com. If you want to discuss the
inspection date, call me at (612) 555-0100.
Sincerely,
S. Rennick
Commissioning, DER Program Office
Alleniom Utilities

ALLENIOM UTILITIES
DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
(612) 555-0100 · der.program@alleniom.com · alleniom.com


July 14, 2025
Ms. Imogen Strathe
Project Manager
Halbray Community Solar LP
6120 Halbray Road
Kelloway Township, Alleron 07KT

Re: Pre-PTO backfeed request — Halbray Field Solar Site 3 (PXA-2024-0002),
feeder ALN-159 — requested date July 29, 2025
Dear Ms. Strathe:
We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025. The gating
item is the final electrical approval from Kelloway Township. Permit EP-25-0418 states
that no permitted work shall be energized before final approval, and the final inspection
is only booked for July 24, 2025; no final approval is in the record yet. If the Township
passes the inspection and issues final approval on July 24, 2025, and the items below are
closed, we can support energization on July 29, 2025. If final approval is not issued by
July 24, 2025, we cannot energize on July 29, 2025; we will re-date the request with
Distribution Operations.
Basis for this answer
The executed ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3 (11/18/2024) permits pre-PTO backfeed on your
written request: the Company may energize the customer's facilities from the feeder for
construction and commissioning power before PTO, provided the generating facility stays
disabled and does not operate in parallel, with Distribution Operations performing the
switching under its own switching order. Your July 9, 2025 letter is that written request,
and it confirms the inverters will remain disabled.
The controlling limit here is the permit, not the ISA. Kelloway Township permit EP-25-
0418 (issued 05/12/2025) adopts the 2023 NEC and states: “No permitted work shall be
energized before final approval.” The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the
ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection.
The backfeed would energize that work. Your letter and our commissioning checklist
record the final inspection as booked for July 24, 2025; the permit itself records only that
it is booked by the permit holder, and no final approval has been issued.
The ISA capacity is 2.3 MW ac (2,300 kW), matching the four 575 kW skids and the
permit scope. The equipment records show the ratings are adequate: T-1 is 2,500 kVA,
13.2 kV to 800Y/462 V, 5.75%, giving 1,804 A secondary full-load current and 31.4 kA at
CSB-1 against 65 kA switchgear; the 150E primary fuses are at 137% of the 109 A
primary full-load current (NEC 450.3(A) limit 300%); the 2,000 A secondary main is at
111% of 1,804 A (limit 125%); the highest-voltage-drop collection feeder, C-4, is 1.49%;
and the measured ground resistance is 3.1 ohms. No rating or ampacity exception was
found.
What is already in order for the backfeed
 Construction is complete 07/03/2025; equipment schedules E-201 and E-301 Rev B
  (06/20/2025) record the four 575 kW skids, the 800 V collection system, CSB-1, T-1
  and the 13.2 kV primary switch.
 The utility RTU end-to-end point-to-point test was accepted on 07/02/2025 (TCS-02
  §3.6). The POI recloser settings and protection coordination study were issued on
  06/16/2025, and site acceptance items 1 to 7 were accepted in writing on 07/07/2025
    (DPS-07 §5.1 and §6.2); those items are owned by Distribution Protection Engineering
   and are not re-reviewed here.
 Revenue meter RM-0002 was set on 07/08/2025; Metering will confirm its final test
   and seal before switching. The installed inverters, NG-XT-225 (eight) and NG-XT-125
   (four), are in the body of the current CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025).
The witness test and the SOC's live-telemetry confirmation are conditions of PTO, not of
the pre-PTO backfeed; they do not stand in the way of July 29.
What must be closed before July 29, 2025
1. Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors
   Inc. (the permit holder). Pass the final inspection on 07/24/2025 and send the written
   final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office as soon as it is issued, and in
   any event before the switching order is released. If the inspection is postponed, fails,
   or is not followed by written approval, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
2. Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock
   AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send us
   the isolation procedure and the signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the
   generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed.
3. Two construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection —
   Tamsworth. These are confirmations, not additional utility requirements if the
   installed work already complies; they need to be in the record so they do not become a
   second gate at the final inspection:
     (a) CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal
        voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. NEC
        2023 110.16(B) requires those fields. The label should also carry the arc-flash
        boundary and either the incident energy at the working distance or the PPE
        category needed for the contractor's energized-work procedure. Confirm the
        installed label carries them, or replace it.
     (b) Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in
        rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit
        single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from
        underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and
        marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method.
Path to July 29, 2025
If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025,
Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching
window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control the actual
switching. If any item slips, we will give you the next available date.
Scope of this letter
This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings,
coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue position, and the system
impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not re-reviewed here.
Witness test and SOC live telemetry remain PTO conditions.
Please send the final approval and the isolation confirmation to me at
s.rennick@alleniom.com, copied to der.program@alleniom.com. If you want to discuss the
inspection date, call me at (612) 555-0100.
Sincerely,
S. Rennick
Commissioning, DER Program Office
Alleniom Utilities
s.rennick@alleniom.com · (612) 555-0100

What is already in order for the backfeed
 Construction is complete 07/03/2025; equipment schedules E-201 and E-301 Rev B
  (06/20/2025) record the four 575 kW skids, the 800 V collection system, CSB-1, T-1 and
  the 13.2 kV primary switch.
 The utility RTU end-to-end point-to-point test was accepted on 07/02/2025 (TCS-02 §3.6).
  The POI recloser settings and protection coordination study were issued on 06/16/2025,
  and site acceptance items 1 to 7 were accepted in writing on 07/07/2025 (DPS-07 §5.1 and
  §6.2); those items are owned by Distribution Protection Engineering and are not re-
  reviewed here.
 Revenue meter RM-0002 was set 07/08/2025; Alleniom Metering will confirm its test and
  seal before switching. The installed inverters, NG-XT-225 (eight) and NG-XT-125 (four),
  are in the body of the current CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025).
 The witness test and the SOC's live-telemetry confirmation are conditions of PTO, not of the
pre-PTO backfeed; they do not stand in the way of July 29.
What must be closed before July 29, 2025
1. Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc.
   (the permit holder). Confirm the 07/24/2025 booking with the Township now, pass the final
   inspection, and send the written final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office
   when issued and before the switching order is released. If the inspection is postponed,
   fails, or is not followed by written approval, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
2. Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock
   AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send the
   isolation procedure and signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the generating
   facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed. Without that
   confirmation, we will not release the switching order.
3. Two construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection — Tamsworth.
   These are confirmations, not additional utility requirements if the installed work already
   complies; they need to be in the record so they do not become a second gate at the final
   inspection:
     (a) CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal
        voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. NEC 2023
        110.16(B) requires those fields. The label should also carry the arc-flash boundary and
        either the incident energy at the working distance or the PPE category required for
        energized work. Confirm the installed label carries them, or replace it.
     (b) Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in rigid
        steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit single-rated
        USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from underground to a terminal.
        Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and marked for the application, or
        replace it with a permitted wiring method. If these two points are not confirmed, the
        final inspection may fail, and July 29 cannot hold.
Path to July 29, 2025
If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025,
Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window.
Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control switching. If any item
slips, we will give you the next available date.
Scope of this letter
This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed and is not a permission to operate. RTU/POI
recloser acceptance, settings, coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue
position, and the system impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not re-
reviewed here; witness test and SOC live telemetry remain PTO conditions.

s.rennick@alleniom.com, copied to der.program@alleniom.com. If you want to discuss the
inspection date, call me at (612) 555-0100.

S. Rennick

Alleniom Utilities

Re:  Pre-PTO backfeed request — Halbray Field Solar Site 3 (PXA-2024-0002), feeder ALN-159 — requested date July 29, 2025
We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025. The gating item is the final electrical approval from Kelloway Township. Permit EP-25-0418 states that no permitted work shall be energized before final approval, and the final inspection is only booked for July 24, 2025; no final approval is in the record yet. If the Township passes the inspection and issues final approval on July 24, 2025, and the items below are closed, we can support energization on July 29, 2025. If final approval is not issued by July 24, 2025, we cannot energize on July 29, 2025; we will re-date the request with Distribution Operations.
The controlling limit here is the permit, not the ISA. Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 (issued 05/12/2025) adopts the 2023 NEC and states: “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval.” The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The backfeed would energize that work. Your letter and our commissioning checklist record the final inspection as booked for July 24, 2025; the permit itself records only that it is booked by the permit holder, and no final approval has been issued.
The ISA capacity is 2.3 MW ac (2,300 kW), matching the four 575 kW skids and the permit scope; the request does not change the executed capacity or point of interconnection. The equipment records show the ratings are adequate: T-1 is 2,500 kVA, 13.2 kV to 800Y/462 V, 5.75%, giving 1,804 A secondary full-load current and 31.4 kA at CSB-1 against 65 kA switchgear; the 150E primary fuses are at 137% of the 109 A primary full-load current (NEC 450.3(A) limit 300%); the 2,000 A secondary main is at 111% of 1,804 A (limit 125%); the highest-voltage-drop collection feeder, C-4, is 1.49%; and the measured ground resistance is 3.1 ohms. No rating or ampacity exception was found.
The witness test and the SOC's live-telemetry confirmation are conditions of PTO, not of the pre-PTO backfeed; they do not stand in the way of July 29.
What must be closed before July 29, 2025
Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. (the permit holder). Confirm the 07/24/2025 booking with the Township now, pass the final inspection, and send the written final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office when issued and before the switching order is released. If the inspection is postponed, fails, or is not followed by written approval, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
(a)  CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. NEC 2023 110.16(B) requires those fields. The label should also carry the arc-flash boundary and either the incident energy at the working distance or the PPE category required for energized work (NFPA 70E 130.5(H)). Confirm the installed label carries them, or replace it.
(b)  Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method. If these two points are not confirmed, the final inspection may fail, and July 29 cannot hold.
Path to July 29, 2025
If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025, Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control switching. If any item slips, we will give you the next available date.
This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed and is not a permission to operate. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings, coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue position, and the system impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not reviewed here; witness test and SOC live telemetry remain PTO conditions.

14 'Normal' We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025. The gating item is the final electrical approval from Kelloway Township. Permit EP-25-0418 states that no permitted work shall be energized before final approval, and the final inspection is only booked for July 24, 2025; no final approval is in the record yet. If the Township passes the inspection and issues final approval on July 24, 2025, and the items below are closed, we can support energization on July 29, 2025. If final approval is not issued by July 24, 2025, we cannot energize on July 29, 2025; we will re-date the request with Distribution Operations.
15 'Normal' Basis for this answer
16 'Normal' The executed ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3 (11/18/2024) permits pre-PTO backfeed on your written request: the Company may energize the customer's facilities from the feeder for construction and commissioning power before PTO, provided the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel, with Distribution Operations switching under its own order. Your July 9, 2025 letter is that written request, and it confirms the inverters will remain disabled.
17 'Normal' The controlling limit here is the permit, not the ISA. Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 (issued 05/12/2025) adopts the 2023 NEC and states: “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval.” The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The backfeed would energize that work. Your letter and our commissioning checklist record the final inspection as booked for July 24, 2025; the permit itself records only that it is booked by the permit holder, and no final approval has been issued.
18 'Normal' The ISA capacity is 2.3 MW ac (2,300 kW), matching the four 575 kW skids and the permit scope; the request does not change the executed capacity or point of interconnection. The equipment records show the ratings are adequate: T-1 is 2,500 kVA, 13.2 kV to 800Y/462 V, 5.75%, giving 1,804 A secondary full-load current and 31.4 kA at CSB-1 against 65 kA switchgear; the 150E primary fuses are at 137% of the 109 A primary full-load current (NEC 450.3(A) limit 300%); the 2,000 A secondary main is at 111% of 1,804 A (limit 125%); the highest-voltage-drop collection feeder, C-4, is 1.49%; and the measured ground resistance is 3.1 ohms. No rating or ampacity exception was found in those records.
19 'Normal' What is already in order for the backfeed
20 'List Bullet' Construction is complete 07/03/2025; equipment schedules E-201 and E-301 Rev B (06/20/2025) record the four 575 kW skids, the 800 V collection system, CSB-1, T-1 and the 13.2 kV primary switch.
21 'List Bullet' The utility RTU end-to-end point-to-point test was accepted on 07/02/2025 (TCS-02 §3.6). The POI recloser settings and protection coordination study were issued on 06/16/2025, and site acceptance items 1 to 7 were accepted in writing on 07/07/2025 (DPS-07 §5.1 and §6.2); those items are owned by Distribution Protection Engineering and are not reviewed here.
22 'List Bullet' Revenue meter RM-0002 was set 07/08/2025; Alleniom Metering will confirm its test and seal before switching. The installed inverters, NG-XT-225 (eight) and NG-XT-125 (four), are in the body of the current CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025).
23 'Normal' The witness test and the SOC's live-telemetry confirmation are conditions of PTO, not of the pre-PTO backfeed; they do not stand in the way of July 29.
24 'Normal' What must be closed before July 29, 2025
25 'List Number' Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. (the permit holder). Confirm the 07/24/2025 booking with the Township now, pass the final inspection, and send the written final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office when issued and before the switching order is released. If the inspection is postponed, fails, or is not followed by written approval, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
26 'List Number' Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send the isolation procedure and signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed. Without that confirmation, we will not release the switching order.
27 'List Number' Two construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection — Tamsworth. These are confirmations, not additional utility requirements if the installed work already complies; they need to be in the record so they do not become a second gate at the final inspection:
28 'Normal' (a)  CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. NEC 2023 110.16(B) requires those fields. The label should also carry the arc-flash boundary and either the incident energy at the working distance or the PPE category required for energized work (NFPA 70E 130.5(H)). Confirm the installed label carries them, or replace it.
29 'Normal' (b)  Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method. If these two points are not confirmed, the final inspection may fail, and July 29 cannot hold.
30 'Normal' Path to July 29, 2025
31 'Normal' If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025, Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control switching. If any item slips, we will give you the next available date.
32 'Normal' Scope of this letter
33 'Normal' This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed and is not a permission to operate. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings, coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue position, and the system impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not reviewed here; witness test and SOC live telemetry remain PTO conditions.
34 'Normal' Please send the final approval and the isolation confirmation to me at s.rennick@alleniom.com, copied to der.program@alleniom.com. If you want to discuss the inspection date, call me at (612) 555-0100.
35 'Normal' Sincerely,

§1 Purpose and Scope
This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
defined in §3.
DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:
• classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
• eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
• recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
• protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);

• treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).
This standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both
this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.
§2 References
The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
applies.
• IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
• DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution
protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
facilities.
• TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU
installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
for permission to operate.
• CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL
3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.
• ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards 
§3 DER Classification
DER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with
IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.
Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.
Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility
interconnection practice.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.
§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.
§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.
§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.
§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.
§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.


--- page 4 ---
DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard
Page 4
DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1.  Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2.  Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.
§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1.  A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2.  An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
• Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
• POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
additional utility hardware.
Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.
No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.
Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
certification and Control Narrative are always required.


--- page 5 ---

Page 5
DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
§4 Screening and Study Process
Applications in DER Program scope proceed through initial technical screening under Interconnection Studies.
Facilities not passing initial screens may be evaluated under supplemental review per SRP-3 or advance to a system
impact study. This standard does not restate SRP-3; the daytime minimum-load convention and other screen
methodologies are prescribed there.

2.  Table 5-1 addresses protective and control equipment. Monitoring and communications requirements are
established under TCS-02.
3.  Where §3.6 recognition is in effect at a pure-generation site with a utility POI recloser, the ANSI 32
directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips on violation.
§6 Monitoring and Control
Facilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through
a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5
for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.
Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.
§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
§8 Records and Compliance
Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

standard and another Alleniom operating standard encountered in screening or study is referred to per-site
engineering determination under ERP-9 §3.
End of DIS-01 Rev 4.
