# Independent review — Halbray pre-PTO backfeed reply and OpenProject work package

As-of date: 07/14/2025. Deliverables reviewed: `/filesystem/Halbray_Backfeed_Reply.docx`; OpenProject work package #47 in `DER Program Backlog Review` (project 3). Source records re-read directly from `/filesystem` and `/tmp/ahpele/corpus`; key numbers recomputed independently.

## Findings (most serious first)

### 1. BLOCKING — Missed NEC 250.122 equipment-grounding-conductor violation in the ac collection feeders that the backfeed energizes
- **Requirement:** Permit EP-25-0418 adopts NFPA 70, 2023 edition (`Correspondence/2025-05-12_Kelloway_Township_Electrical_Permit_EP-25-0418.pdf`, “Adopted code”). NEC 2023 Table 250.122 requires a copper equipment grounding conductor of **2/0 AWG** for a circuit protected by a **600 A** overcurrent device. NEC 250.122(F) requires a full-size EGC in each parallel raceway.
- **What the deliverable has:** The letter says “No rating or ampacity exception was found in those records” (p.1) and lists only two construction-record confirmations — CSB-1 arc-flash label and inverter ac output cable USE-2 — in the letter (p.2) and in work package #47 (items 3 and 4). It does not mention the collection-feeder EGC.
- **What it should be:** The letter and work package must identify that collection feeders C-1 to C-4 are recorded with **1 AWG Cu** EGC in each duct, protected by **600 A** breakers in CSB-1, and that 1 AWG is two standard sizes below the **2/0 AWG Cu** required by Table 250.122. Tamsworth must upsize/replace the EGC to 2/0 Cu (or provide a code-compliant design) and document it before the final inspection/backfeed.
- **Evidence:** `Equipment/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx`, sheet “Collection Feeders”, rows C-1 to C-4: “Equipment grounding conductor = 1 AWG Cu in each duct”; “Overcurrent protection = 600 A breaker in CSB-1”. All four feeders are the same. The backfeed energizes these feeders: Halbray request (07/09/2025) asks to energize the step-up transformer and ac collection system; the letter (p.1) says the backfeed energizes the ac collection system. The 600 A breakers are the OCPDs protecting the feeders, so Table 250.122 gives 2/0 Cu, not 1 AWG. This is a hard code non-conformance in work that will be energized even with the inverters isolated at AD-1 to AD-4.

### 2. MAJOR — The letter and work package impose a 07/24/2025 final-approval deadline that the permit does not
- **Requirement:** Kelloway permit EP-25-0418: “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval.” The permit does **not** require final approval by 07/24/2025; 07/24/2025 is the booked final-inspection date (Halbray letter 07/09/2025; CX-HB-03).
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.1: “If final approval is not issued by July 24, 2025, we cannot energize on July 29, 2025.” Work package #47: “If approval is not issued by 2025-07-24 or the inspection fails, 2025-07-29 cannot hold.”
- **What it should be:** The permit condition is satisfied by written final approval **before the switching order is released / before energization on 07/29/2025**, not necessarily by 07/24/2025. If the 07/24 inspection passes and written approval issues on 07/25–07/28, 07/29 remains feasible. The letter’s own item 1 correctly says “send the written final approval … when issued and before the switching order is released” (p.2), which contradicts the p.1 absolute 07/24 cutoff. The work package should use the same condition and a due date that does not treat 07/24 as the approval deadline.
- **Evidence:** Permit EP-25-0418 (final inspection “Booked by the permit holder”; “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval”); Halbray request (inspection booked 07/24/2025); CX-HB-03 (AHJ final inspection booked 07/24/2025). No document makes 07/24/2025 the final-approval deadline.

### 3. MAJOR — The 13.2 kV interconnection conductor rating/ampacity is not in the construction record, so “no rating or ampacity exception” is unsupported for that part of the energized work
- **Requirement/record:** Permit scope includes “its 13.2 kV interconnection.” The backfeed energizes T-1 and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The equipment schedule lists PSW-1 (15 kV, 600 A, 150E fuses) but contains no 13.2 kV cable/conductor schedule, ampacity, EGC/shielding, or test record. The commissioning checklist has no 13.2 kV cable test.
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.1: “No rating or ampacity exception was found in those records.” It cites only T-1, the 150E fuses, the 2,000 A main, C-4 voltage drop and ground resistance. The “already in order” bullet says the equipment schedules record the “13.2 kV primary switch,” not the 13.2 kV cable. Work package #47 likewise lists the “13.2 kV primary switch” in “Already in order” but does not list the 13.2 kV cable record or a confirmation.
- **What it should be:** Either confirm the 13.2 kV interconnection conductors and their rating/ampacity from a construction record, or state that the record is missing and require Tamsworth to provide it before the final inspection/backfeed. Do not state that all ratings are adequate without the 13.2 kV conductor record.
- **Evidence:** `Equipment/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx` (no 13.2 kV cable row; only PSW-1, T-1, CSB-1, AUX-1, RM-0002, POI, GND, Labels and 800 V C-1 to C-4); permit scope; Halbray request (energize step-up transformer and ac collection system); CX-HB-03 (no 13.2 kV cable item). If the 13.2 kV cable is utility-owned under the POI-recloser scope, the record should say so; it does not.

### 4. MINOR — The 800 V collection-feeder phase conductors are at the 75 °C ampacity limit, with no soil/termination basis in the record
- **Requirement:** NEC 2023 310.15/110.14(C) — conductor ampacity must be corrected for conditions of use and limited by termination temperature.
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.1: “No rating or ampacity exception was found in those records.” The schedule gives 2 sets of 3 × 1/C 350 kcmil Cu, 2 kV RHW-2, 600 A breaker, but gives only voltage drop, no ampacity calculation, soil temperature/thermal resistivity, or termination rating.
- **What it should be:** Tamsworth should provide the ampacity calculation for the 2 × 350 kcmil Cu feeders. At 75 °C, 2 × 350 kcmil Cu = 620 A vs the 600 A breaker (3.3 % margin); a 0.95 soil/ambient correction would reduce it below 600 A. At 90 °C the value is 700 A. The record must show which basis applies before the letter says there is no ampacity exception.
- **Evidence:** `Equipment/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx`, “Collection Feeders”, C-1 to C-4 (2 × 3 × 1/C 350 kcmil Cu, 600 A breaker; no ampacity/correction data). NEC Table 310.16: 350 kcmil Cu 75 °C = 310 A; 90 °C = 350 A.

### 5. MINOR — The letter says the backfeed would energize the four inverter skids; they are isolated at AD-1 to AD-4
- **Requirement/record:** Halbray request: “The inverters stay disabled throughout the backfeed and will not operate in parallel before permission to operate.” ISA summary: during a backfeed “the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel.” The letter itself (item 2) requires AD-1 to AD-4 open and locked.
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.1: “The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The backfeed would energize that work.”
- **What it should be:** The backfeed energizes the ac collection system and T-1 up to the open AD-1 to AD-4; the inverter skids and their ac output cables are isolated and are not energized. The permit still gates the backfeed because the collection system and transformer are permitted work, but the sentence overstates what is energized.
- **Evidence:** `Equipment/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Inverter_Skid_Schedule.xlsx`, sheets “Skids” and “Disconnects”: inverters → ACP → AD-1 to AD-4 (600 A fused, padlockable) → collection feeder. ADs open/locked isolate the skids. Halbray request (07/09/2025); ISA summary pre-PTO backfeed term.

### 6. MINOR — Wrong NEC clause/content for the CSB-1 arc-flash label
- **Requirement:** Permit adopts NEC 2023. NEC 2023 110.16(B) is limited to equipment **rated 600 V, nominal, or less**; CSB-1 is **800 V**. The general arc-flash warning is NEC 110.16(A); the label content (arc-flash boundary plus incident energy/PPE category) is NFPA 70E 130.5(H). The 2023 NEC 110.16(B) content is not the old “available fault current, clearing time, date” set the letter recites.
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.2 and work package #47 item 3: “NEC 2023 110.16(B) requires those fields” (nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time, date), then says the label “should also carry” the arc-flash boundary and incident energy/PPE category.
- **What it should be:** Cite NEC 110.16(A) and NFPA 70E 130.5(H) for the label content; if 110.16(B) is cited, note that it does not apply at 800 V. The substantive requirement (label must carry the boundary and incident energy/PPE category) is still valid and should remain in the letter/work package.
- **Evidence:** `Equipment/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx`, “Equipment” row CSB-1 (800 V; 2,500 A bus); row Labels (records only nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time, calculation date). NEC 2023 110.16(B) voltage limit; CSB-1 800 V.

### 7. MINOR — The “Path to July 29” omits the construction-record confirmations
- **Requirement/instruction:** Tell the customer what has to be done before 07/29 and by whom; the letter’s own item 3 makes the arc-flash and USE-2 confirmations pre-inspection conditions.
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.2: “If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025, Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window.” Only two of the four listed items are named.
- **What it should be:** The path should include all conditions (final approval, isolation/lockout, arc-flash label confirmation, USE-2 confirmation, and the EGC correction above) or refer to “all items in the list.” As written, a reader could think the construction-record confirmations are not needed for the path.
- **Evidence:** Letter p.2 items 1–3 vs. “Path to July 29” paragraph.

### 8. MINOR — Revenue-meter test/seal is described as a pre-switching action but is not tracked as a condition
- **Requirement/record:** ISA summary: revenue meter RM-0002 at the point of interconnection. CX-HB-03: meter set by Alleniom Metering 07/08/2025. The letter itself says “Alleniom Metering will confirm its test and seal before switching.”
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.1 bullet: “Revenue meter RM-0002 was set 07/08/2025; Alleniom Metering will confirm its test and seal before switching.” It is not in the numbered “What must be closed” list or in work package #47.
- **What it should be:** If the meter test/seal is a switching prerequisite, list it with owner (Alleniom Metering) and due date, or state that the meter is already accepted and no confirmation is outstanding. No test/seal record is in the file.
- **Evidence:** `Commissioning/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Commissioning_Checklist.pdf` (meter set 07/08/2025 only); `Contracts/ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3_Executed_Summary.pdf` (RM-0002 at POI); letter p.1 and p.2 list.

### 9. MINOR — “Construction is complete 07/03/2025” is the customer’s report, not an independent field record
- **Requirement/record:** The only source is Halbray’s 07/09/2025 request (“Construction was completed on 07/03/2025”). CX-HB-03 does not record a construction-complete date or field verification.
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.2: “Construction is complete 07/03/2025.”
- **What it should be:** Attribute it: “Halbray reports construction complete 07/03/2025,” or verify it from a field/commissioning record. The AHJ final inspection is still pending.
- **Evidence:** `Correspondence/2025-07-09_Halbray_Backfeed_Request.pdf`; `Commissioning/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Commissioning_Checklist.pdf` (no construction-complete entry).

### 10. MINOR — Signer/contact not in the DER Program Contact Directory
- **Requirement/record:** The contact directory lists program contacts but has no S. Rennick or s.rennick@alleniom.com. The commissioning checklist names S. Rennick as coordinator, so the person exists on the record, but the direct email/phone in the letter is not corroborated by the directory.
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter signature block “S. Rennick, Commissioning, DER Program Office, s.rennick@alleniom.com · (612) 555-0100”; cc Tamsworth.
- **What it should be:** Confirm the signer’s title/email/phone against the directory or add the signer to the directory; use the shared program inbox/phone if that is the established contact. Not a substantive defect in the determination.
- **Evidence:** `DER_Program_Contact_Directory.xlsx` (no S. Rennick; shared inbox der.program@alleniom.com, main (612) 555-0100); CX-HB-03 coordinator line.

### 11. MINOR — Requirements register source-candidate column is incomplete for rows that do have candidate IDs
- **Instruction:** “Record each hard requirement in /tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv with a column citing the candidate IDs it comes from.”
- **What the deliverable has:** `requirements.csv` has a `source_candidate_ids` column, but it is blank for e.g. REQ-PER-01/02/03/04 (permit candidate R0108) and EQ-DC (candidate R0154); the author cites those IDs only in the note text for some rows.
- **What it should be:** Put the candidate ID(s) in the `source_candidate_ids` column for rows that came from a scanned candidate; reserve blank for table/drawing requirements with no candidate. The `ahpele_reqscan.py --check` passes (68/68 reviewed), so this is a register-format completeness issue, not an unreviewed candidate.
- **Evidence:** `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv` rows REQ-PER-01 to 04, EQ-DC; req_candidates.md R0108 and R0154.

### 12. MINOR — The CEL check is listed under “already in order for the backfeed,” but it is a PTO/witness-test item
- **Requirement/record:** ENG-PRC-014 §3/§4.1 makes CEL listing an eligibility input to the witness-test waiver, and CX-HB-03 records the witness-test determination “at the permission-to-operate request.” TCS-02 §5 makes live telemetry a PTO condition.
- **What the deliverable has:** Letter p.2, “What is already in order for the backfeed”: “The installed inverters … are in the body of the current CEL-2025-Q2.” The next sentence correctly says the witness test and SOC live telemetry are PTO conditions, not backfeed conditions.
- **What it should be:** Move the CEL statement to the PTO/witness-test discussion or label it as a PTO item. It does not stand in the way of the 07/29 backfeed.
- **Evidence:** ENG-PRC-014 §3/§4.1; CX-HB-03 (witness-test determination at PTO); letter p.2 bullet and following paragraph.

## Items checked and found acceptable (brief)
- Letter is a valid DOCX, 2 pages; `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py` reports no format problems.
- Direct answer: “We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025” — correct as of 07/14 because no AHJ final approval is in the record.
- Permit quote and permit scope (2.3 MW ac; four skids; ac collection; 2,500 kVA T-1; 13.2 kV interconnection) match EP-25-0418.
- ISA pre-PTO backfeed term, capacity (2.3 MW ac / 2,300 kW), feeder ALN-159 and requirements for written request/inverters disabled/no parallel/Distribution Operations switching match the executed ISA summary.
- Values checked and matching: 4 × 575 kW = 2,300 kW; T-1 2,500 kVA at 800 V → 1,804 A; 1,804/0.0575 → 31.4 kA vs 65 kA; 2,500 kVA at 13.2 kV → 109 A; 150/109 = 137 %; 2,000/1,804 = 111 %; C-4 1.49 %; ground resistance 3.1 ohm.
- RTU end-to-end test 07/02/2025, POI settings/coordination 06/16/2025, site acceptance items 1–7 on 07/07/2025, meter set 07/08/2025 match CX-HB-03.
- Inverters NG-XT-225 (8) and NG-XT-125 (4) are in the body of CEL-2025-Q2 (not just front matter/footnote).

Dear Ms. Strathe:
We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025. The gating item is the final electrical approval from Kelloway Township. Permit EP-25-0418 states that no permitted work shall be energized before final approval, and the final inspection is only booked for July 24, 2025; no final approval is in the record yet. If the Township passes the inspection and issues final approval on July 24, 2025, and the items below are closed, we can support energization on July 29, 2025. If final approval is not issued by July 24, 2025, we cannot energize on July 29, 2025; we will re-date the request with Distribution Operations.
Basis for this answer
The executed ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3 (11/18/2024) permits pre-PTO backfeed on your written request: the Company may energize the customer's facilities from the feeder for construction and commissioning power before PTO, provided the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel, with Distribution Operations switching under its own order. Your July 9, 2025 letter is that written request, and it confirms the inverters will remain disabled.
The controlling limit here is the permit, not the ISA. Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 (issued 05/12/2025) adopts the 2023 NEC and states: “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval.” The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The backfeed would energize that work. Your letter and our commissioning checklist record the final inspection as booked for July 24, 2025; the permit itself records only that it is booked by the permit holder, and no final approval has been issued.
The ISA capacity is 2.3 MW ac (2,300 kW), matching the four 575 kW skids and the permit scope; the request does not change the executed capacity or point of interconnection. The equipment records show the ratings are adequate: T-1 is 2,500 kVA, 13.2 kV to 800Y/462 V, 5.75%, giving 1,804 A secondary full-load current and 31.4 kA at CSB-1 against 65 kA switchgear; the 150E primary fuses are at 137% of the 109 A primary full-load current (NEC 450.3(A) limit 300%); the 2,000 A secondary main is at 111% of 1,804 A (limit 125%); the highest-voltage-drop collection feeder, C-4, is 1.49%; and the measured ground resistance is 3.1 ohms. No rating or ampacity exception was found in those records.
What is already in order for the backfeed
Construction is complete 07/03/2025; equipment schedules E-201 and E-301 Rev B (06/20/2025) record the four 575 kW skids, the 800 V collection system, CSB-1, T-1 and the 13.2 kV primary switch.
The utility RTU end-to-end point-to-point test was accepted on 07/02/2025 (TCS-02 §3.6). The POI recloser settings and protection coordination study were issued on 06/16/2025, and site acceptance items 1 to 7 were accepted in writing on 07/07/2025 (DPS-07 §5.1 and §6.2); those items are owned by Distribution Protection Engineering and are not reviewed here.
Revenue meter RM-0002 was set 07/08/2025; Alleniom Metering will confirm its test and seal before switching. The installed inverters, NG-XT-225 (eight) and NG-XT-125 (four), are in the body of the current CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025).
The witness test and the SOC's live-telemetry confirmation are conditions of PTO, not of the pre-PTO backfeed; they do not stand in the way of July 29.
What must be closed before July 29, 2025
Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. (the permit holder). Confirm the 07/24/2025 booking with the Township now, pass the final inspection, and send the written final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office when issued and before the switching order is released. If the inspection is postponed, fails, or is not followed by written approval, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send the isolation procedure and signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed. Without that confirmation, we will not release the switching order.
Two construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection — Tamsworth. These are confirmations, not additional utility requirements if the installed work already complies; they need to be in the record so they do not become a second gate at the final inspection:
(a)  CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. NEC 2023 110.16(B) requires those fields. The label should also carry the arc-flash boundary and either the incident energy at the working distance or the PPE category required for energized work (NFPA 70E 130.5(H)). Confirm the installed label carries them, or replace it.
(b)  Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method. If these two points are not confirmed, the final inspection may fail, and July 29 cannot hold.
Path to July 29, 2025
If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025, Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control switching. If any item slips, we will give you the next available date.
Scope of this letter
This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed and is not a permission to operate. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings, coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue position, and the system impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not reviewed here; witness test and SOC live telemetry remain PTO conditions.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

doc = Document()
for section in doc.sections:
    section.top_margin = Inches(0.6)
    section.bottom_margin = Inches(0.6)
    section.left_margin = Inches(0.9)
    section.right_margin = Inches(0.9)

style = doc.styles['Normal']
style.font.name = 'Calibri'
style.font.size = Pt(10.25)
style.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
style.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 0.98

def para(text="", bold=False, size=None, space_before=0, space_after=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
    if space_after is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.bold = bold
    if size:
        r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p

def heading(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(5)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.bold = True
    r.font.size = Pt(10.25)
    return p

def bullet(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet')
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.25)
    p.add_run(text)
    return p

def numbered(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style='List Number')
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.25)
    p.add_run(text)
    return p

def subitem(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.55)
    p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.2)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    p.add_run(text)
    return p

def hr():
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pBdr = OxmlElement('w:pBdr')
    bottom = OxmlElement('w:bottom')
    bottom.set(qn('w:val'), 'single')
    bottom.set(qn('w:sz'), '8')
    bottom.set(qn('w:space'), '1')
    bottom.set(qn('w:color'), '1F4E79')
    pBdr.append(bottom)
    pPr.append(pBdr)

# Letterhead
p = para("ALLENIOM UTILITIES", bold=True, size=15, space_after=0)
p.runs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F,0x4E,0x79)
para("DER Program Office", bold=True, size=11, space_after=0)
para("4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA", size=9, space_after=0)
para("(612) 555-0100  ·  der.program@alleniom.com  ·  alleniom.com", size=9, space_after=0)
hr()

para("July 14, 2025", space_after=7)
for line in ["Ms. Imogen Strathe", "Project Manager", "Halbray Community Solar LP",
             "6120 Halbray Road", "Kelloway Township, Alleron 07KT"]:
    para(line, space_after=0)

para("", space_after=1)
p = doc.add_paragraph()
p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(3)
p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(7)
r = p.add_run("Re:  Pre-PTO backfeed request — Halbray Field Solar Site 3 (PXA-2024-0002), feeder ALN-159 — requested date July 29, 2025")
r.bold = True

para("Dear Ms. Strathe:", space_after=5)

para("We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025. The gating item is the final electrical approval from Kelloway Township. Permit EP-25-0418 states that no permitted work shall be energized before final approval, and the final inspection is only booked for July 24, 2025; no final approval is in the record yet. If the Township passes the inspection and issues final approval on July 24, 2025, and the items below are closed, we can support energization on July 29, 2025. If final approval is not issued by July 24, 2025, we cannot energize on July 29, 2025; we will re-date the request with Distribution Operations.")

heading("Basis for this answer")
para("The executed ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3 (11/18/2024) permits pre-PTO backfeed on your written request: the Company may energize the customer's facilities from the feeder for construction and commissioning power before PTO, provided the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel, with Distribution Operations switching under its own order. Your July 9, 2025 letter is that written request, and it confirms the inverters will remain disabled.")
para("The controlling limit here is the permit, not the ISA. Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 (issued 05/12/2025) adopts the 2023 NEC and states: “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval.” The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The backfeed would energize that work. Your letter and our commissioning checklist record the final inspection as booked for July 24, 2025; the permit itself records only that it is booked by the permit holder, and no final approval has been issued.")
para("The ISA capacity is 2.3 MW ac (2,300 kW), matching the four 575 kW skids and the permit scope; the request does not change the executed capacity or point of interconnection. The equipment records show the ratings are adequate: T-1 is 2,500 kVA, 13.2 kV to 800Y/462 V, 5.75%, giving 1,804 A secondary full-load current and 31.4 kA at CSB-1 against 65 kA switchgear; the 150E primary fuses are at 137% of the 109 A primary full-load current (NEC 450.3(A) limit 300%); the 2,000 A secondary main is at 111% of 1,804 A (limit 125%); the highest-voltage-drop collection feeder, C-4, is 1.49%; and the measured ground resistance is 3.1 ohms. No rating or ampacity exception was found in those records.")

heading("What is already in order for the backfeed")
bullet("Construction is complete 07/03/2025; equipment schedules E-201 and E-301 Rev B (06/20/2025) record the four 575 kW skids, the 800 V collection system, CSB-1, T-1 and the 13.2 kV primary switch.")
bullet("The utility RTU end-to-end point-to-point test was accepted on 07/02/2025 (TCS-02 §3.6). The POI recloser settings and protection coordination study were issued on 06/16/2025, and site acceptance items 1 to 7 were accepted in writing on 07/07/2025 (DPS-07 §5.1 and §6.2); those items are owned by Distribution Protection Engineering and are not reviewed here.")
bullet("Revenue meter RM-0002 was set 07/08/2025; Alleniom Metering will confirm its test and seal before switching. The installed inverters, NG-XT-225 (eight) and NG-XT-125 (four), are in the body of the current CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025).")
para("The witness test and the SOC's live-telemetry confirmation are conditions of PTO, not of the pre-PTO backfeed; they do not stand in the way of July 29.")

heading("What must be closed before July 29, 2025")
numbered("Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. (the permit holder). Confirm the 07/24/2025 booking with the Township now, pass the final inspection, and send the written final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office when issued and before the switching order is released. If the inspection is postponed, fails, or is not followed by written approval, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.")
numbered("Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send the isolation procedure and signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed. Without that confirmation, we will not release the switching order.")
numbered("Two construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection — Tamsworth. These are confirmations, not additional utility requirements if the installed work already complies; they need to be in the record so they do not become a second gate at the final inspection:")
subitem("(a)  CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. NEC 2023 110.16(B) requires those fields. The label should also carry the arc-flash boundary and either the incident energy at the working distance or the PPE category required for energized work (NFPA 70E 130.5(H)). Confirm the installed label carries them, or replace it.")
subitem("(b)  Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method. If these two points are not confirmed, the final inspection may fail, and July 29 cannot hold.")

heading("Path to July 29, 2025")
para("If the written final approval and the isolation confirmation are received by July 24, 2025, Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control switching. If any item slips, we will give you the next available date.")

heading("Scope of this letter")
para("This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed and is not a permission to operate. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings, coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue position, and the system impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not reviewed here; witness test and SOC live telemetry remain PTO conditions.")

para("Please send the final approval and the isolation confirmation to me at s.rennick@alleniom.com, copied to der.program@alleniom.com. If you want to discuss the inspection date, call me at (612) 555-0100.")

para("Sincerely,", space_before=1, space_after=3)
para("S. Rennick", bold=True, space_after=0)
para("Commissioning, DER Program Office", space_after=0)
para("Alleniom Utilities", space_after=0)
para("s.rennick@alleniom.com  ·  (612) 555-0100", size=9, space_after=7)
para("cc:  Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. — permit holder, EP-25-0418", size=9)

doc.core_properties.comments = 'Reply to Imogen Strathe, Halbray Community Solar LP, dated 07/14/2025'

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent check for the Halbray backfeed reply and requirement register."""
import csv, datetime, math, os, re, subprocess, sys

ROOT = "/tmp/ahpele"
DOCX = "/filesystem/Halbray_Backfeed_Reply.docx"
fails = []
warns = []

def fail(msg): fails.append(msg)
def warn(msg): warns.append(msg)

    (["--check"], "coverage"),
]:
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"{ROOT}/bin/ahpele_reqscan.py", *args],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = r.stdout + r.stderr
    print(f"[{label}] {out.strip().splitlines()[0] if out.strip() else 'no output'}")
    if label == "register":
        if "notfound=0" not in out or "multi=0" not in out:
            fail(f"requirements register check failed:\n{out}")
    else:
        if r.returncode != 0 or "0 not reviewed yet" not in out:
            fail(f"requirement coverage check failed:\n{out}")

# ---------- 2. Letter contract ----------
doc = Document(DOCX)
text = "\n".join(p.text for p in doc.paragraphs)
low = text.lower()

required_phrases = {
    "date 07/14/2025": "july 14, 2025",
    "addressee Imogen Strathe": "imogen strathe",
    "Halbray Community Solar LP": "halbray community solar lp",
    "site PXA-2024-0002": "pxa-2024-0002",
    "feeder ALN-159": "aln-159",
    "requested 07/29/2025": "july 29, 2025",
    "ISA pre-PTO backfeed": "isa-halbray-field-site-3",
    "permit EP-25-0418": "ep-25-0418",
    "no energization before final approval": "no permitted work shall be energized before final approval",
    "final inspection 07/24/2025": "july 24, 2025",
    "written final approval": "written final approval",
    "inverter isolation/lockout": "isolation",
    "AD-1 to AD-4": "ad-1 to ad-4",
    "arc-flash label": "arc-flash",
    "USE-2 cable": "use-2",
    "witness test is PTO": "witness test",
    "outside scope note": "scope of this letter",
    "signature S. Rennick": "s. rennick",
}
for label, phrase in required_phrases.items():
    if phrase.lower() not in low:
        fail(f"letter missing: {label} ({phrase!r})")

# Must NOT claim confirmed for 07/29 or invent blockers from separate-review items.
if re.search(r"we (can|will) confirm (july )?29", low):
    fail("letter appears to confirm 07/29 unconditionally")
for forbidden in ["queue is the problem", "system impact study is a blocker", "rtu is not installed"]:
    if forbidden in low:
        fail(f"letter raises an out-of-scope blocker: {forbidden}")

# No placeholder values
if re.search(r"\b(TBD|TBA|TODO|FIXME|XXX+)\b", text, re.I):
    fail("letter contains a placeholder")


# ---------- 3a. Source-record and document-status checks ----------
CORPUS = "/tmp/ahpele/corpus"
def src(rel):
    with open(os.path.join(CORPUS, rel + ".txt"), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
        return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", fh.read())

source_docs = {
    "permit": "Correspondence/2025-05-12_Kelloway_Township_Electrical_Permit_EP-25-0418.pdf",
    "isa": "Contracts/ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3_Executed_Summary.pdf",
    "request": "Correspondence/2025-07-09_Halbray_Backfeed_Request.pdf",
    "checklist": "Commissioning/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Commissioning_Checklist.pdf",

    "inverter": "Equipment/PXA-2024-0002_Halbray_Inverter_Skid_Schedule.xlsx",
    "cel": "Standards/CEL-2025-Q2_Certified_Equipment_List.xlsx",
    "dis": "Standards/DIS-01_Rev4_DER_Interconnection_Standard.pdf",
    "dps": "Standards/DPS-07_Rev2_Distribution_Protection_Standard.pdf",
    "tcs": "Standards/TCS-02_Telemetry_Comms_Standard.pdf",
    "eng": "Standards/Witness_Test_Waiver_Procedure.pdf",
}
texts = {k: src(v) for k, v in source_docs.items()}

source_requirements = [
    ("permit", ["No permitted work shall be energized before final approval", "05/12/2025", "2023", "EP-25-0418", "2,500 kVA", "13.2 kV"]),

    ("checklist", ["07/02/2025", "06/16/2025", "07/07/2025", "07/08/2025", "07/24/2025", "07/29/2025", "NG-XT-225 (8)", "NG-XT-125 (4)", "CEL-2025-Q2"]),
    ("equipment", ["2,500 kVA", "13.2 kV", "800Y/462 V", "5.75", "1804", "31.4", "150E", "109", "2,000 A", "65 kA", "1.49", "3.1"]),
    ("inverter", ["575 kW", "800 V", "415", "162.4", "225", "4/0 AWG", "90.2", "125", "1 AWG", "1000 V", "65 kA"]),
    ("cel", ["04/30/2025", "NG-XT-225", "NG-XT-125", "Supersedes CEL-2024-Q4"]),
    ("dis", ["Rev 4", "03/01/2024", "Supersedes DIS-01 Rev 3"]),
    ("dps", ["Rev 2", "09/15/2023", "Supersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1"]),
    ("tcs", ["Rev 1", "06/01/2021"]),
    ("eng", ["Rev 3", "04/30/2025"]),
]
print("\nSource-record checks:")

    missing = [n for n in needles if n not in texts[key]]
    print(f"  {key:10s}: {'PASS' if not missing else 'FAIL'}")
    if missing:
        print(f"    missing: {missing}")
        fail(f"source record {key} missing {missing}")

# Document status: no cited standard/document is from a superseded folder or a superseded edition.
superseded_markers = ["Standards/Superseded", "CEL-2024-Q4", "DIS-01 Rev 3", "DPS-07 Rev 1"]
for marker in superseded_markers:
    if marker in "\n".join(source_docs.values()):
        fail(f"cited a superseded document marker: {marker}")
print("  document status: PASS (all cited records are current; CEL-2025-Q2 supersedes CEL-2024-Q4)")


# ---------- 3. Engineering checks ----------
# Source values (from the records)
kVA = 2500.0
V_pri_kV = 13.2
V_sec_kV = 0.8
Z = 0.0575
FLA_pri = kVA / (math.sqrt(3) * V_pri_kV)
FLA_sec = kVA / (math.sqrt(3) * V_sec_kV)
I_fault = FLA_sec / Z
fuse_pri = 150.0
main_sec = 2000.0
checks = []

def check(name, value, limit, unit, note="", hard=True):
    util = value / limit if limit else 0.0
    if hard:
        ok = value <= limit + 1e-9
    else:
        ok = abs(value - limit) <= 0.01 * abs(limit) if limit else True
    checks.append((name, value, limit, unit, util, ok, note, hard))
    if hard and not ok:
        fail(f"{name}: {value:.3f} {unit} exceeds {limit:.3f} {unit} (utilisation {util:.3f})")

# Transformer and fault duty
check("Transformer primary FLA", FLA_pri, 109.0, "A", "record value 109 A", hard=False)
check("Transformer secondary FLA", FLA_sec, 1804.0, "A", "record value 1804 A", hard=False)
check("CSB-1 fault current", I_fault/1000.0, 31.4, "kA", "record value 31.4 kA", hard=False)
check("Primary fuse ratio 150E/FLA", fuse_pri/FLA_pri, 3.00, "x FLA", "NEC 450.3(A) fuse limit 300%")
check("Secondary main ratio 2000/FLA", main_sec/FLA_sec, 1.25, "x FLA", "NEC 450.3(A) secondary limit 125%")
check("Fault duty 31.4 kA / 65 kA", (I_fault/1000.0)/65.0, 1.0, "x rating", "65 kA switchgear rating")

# Feeder ampacities at 75 degC (NEC Table 310.16): 350 kcmil Cu = 310 A per set
feeder_amp = 2 * 310.0
for tag, load, length in [("C-1",415.0,165),("C-2",415.0,205),("C-3",415.0,240),("C-4",415.0,275)]:
    check(f"{tag} OCPD 600 A / ampacity", 600.0/feeder_amp, 1.0, "x ampacity", f"{feeder_amp:.0f} A ampacity")
    check(f"{tag} load / ampacity", load/feeder_amp, 1.0, "x ampacity", f"load {load:.0f} A")
# Voltage drop (record values)
for tag, vd in [("C-1",0.89),("C-2",1.11),("C-3",1.30),("C-4",1.49)]:
    check(f"{tag} voltage drop", vd, 3.0, "%", "3% target")

# Inverter circuits: 4/0 Cu 75C = 230 A; 1 AWG Cu 75C = 130 A
check("NG-XT-225 OCPD 225 A / 4/0 ampacity", 225.0/230.0, 1.0, "x ampacity", "4/0 Cu 230 A at 75 C")
check("NG-XT-225 load / ampacity", 162.4/230.0, 1.0, "x ampacity", "162.4 A output")
check("NG-XT-125 OCPD 125 A / 1 AWG ampacity", 125.0/130.0, 1.0, "x ampacity", "1 AWG Cu 130 A at 75 C")
check("NG-XT-125 load / ampacity", 90.2/130.0, 1.0, "x ampacity", "90.2 A output")

cmil = {10:10380, 8:16510, 6:26240, 4:41740, 3:52620, 2:66360, 1:83690, "1/0":105600, "3/0":167800, "4/0":211600}
for tag, ocpd, req, prov in [("600 A feeder",600,1,1),("225 A inverter",225,4,4),("125 A inverter",125,6,4),("30 A auxiliary",30,10,10)]:
    check(f"EGC {tag}: required/provided area", cmil[req]/cmil[prov], 1.0, "x", f"required {req} AWG, provided {prov} AWG")

check("GEC 4/0 vs 3/0 required", cmil["3/0"]/cmil["4/0"], 1.0, "x", "4/0 provided, 3/0 required for >1100 kcmil")
check("Ground ring 2 AWG vs 2 AWG minimum", 2.0/2.0, 1.0, "x", "NEC 250.52(A)(4)")
check("Ground resistance", 3.1, 25.0, "ohm", "NEC 250.53(A)(2) single-electrode threshold")

csb_branch = 4*600 + 30
check("CSB-1 branch breaker sum / 120% bus", csb_branch/(1.2*2500), 1.0, "x", f"{csb_branch} A vs 3000 A")
acp_branch = 2*225 + 125
check("ACP branch breaker sum / 120% bus", acp_branch/(1.2*600), 1.0, "x", f"{acp_branch} A vs 720 A")

# Auxiliary tracker load: 8 blocks x 12 drives x 0.25 kW
aux_kw = 8*12*0.25
aux_a = aux_kw*1000/(math.sqrt(3)*800)
check("Tracker auxiliary load / 30 A feeder", 1.25*aux_a/30.0, 1.0, "x", f"{aux_kw:.1f} kW = {aux_a:.1f} A; 125% = {1.25*aux_a:.1f} A")

# DC cable voltage
check("DC maximum voltage / 2 kV cable", 1500.0/2000.0, 1.0, "x", "1,500 V dc on 2 kV cable")

# Date arithmetic
reply = datetime.date(2025,7,14)
insp = datetime.date(2025,7,24)
backfeed = datetime.date(2025,7,29)
if not (reply < insp < backfeed):
    fail("date order is not reply < inspection < backfeed")
print(f"\nDates: reply {reply} -> inspection {insp} ({(insp-reply).days} calendar days, "
      f"{sum(1 for d in range((insp-reply).days) if (reply+datetime.timedelta(days=d+1)).weekday()<5)} business days); "
      f"inspection -> backfeed {backfeed} ({(backfeed-insp).days} calendar days, "
      f"{sum(1 for d in range((backfeed-insp).days) if (insp+datetime.timedelta(days=d+1)).weekday()<5)} business days)")

# Print worst case per limit group
print("\nEngineering checks (worst case shown per group):")
print(f"{'Check':45s} {'Value':>10s} {'Limit':>10s} {'Util':>7s}  Result")
for name, value, limit, unit, util, ok, note, hard in checks:
    print(f"{name:45s} {value:10.3f} {limit:10.3f} {util:7.3f}  {'PASS' if ok else ('FAIL' if hard else 'INFO')}  {note}")

# Worst utilisation summary (hard limits only)
hard_checks = [c for c in checks if c[7]]
worst = max(hard_checks, key=lambda c: c[4])
print(f"\nWorst hard-limit utilisation: {worst[0]} at {worst[4]:.3f} ({worst[1]:.3f}/{worst[2]:.3f} {worst[3]}).")
if worst[4] > 1.0:
    fail(f"worst utilisation exceeds 1.0: {worst[0]}")

# Report close-to-limit OCPD/ampacity ratios (not failures; existing design)

for w in warns: print(" -", w)

for f in fails: print(" FAIL:", f)

§1 Purpose and Scope
This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
defined in §3.
DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:
• classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
• eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
• recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
• protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);


--- page 2 ---
DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard
Page 2
DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
• treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).
This standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both
this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.
§2 References
The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
applies.
• IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
• DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution
protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
facilities.
• TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU
installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
for permission to operate.
• CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL
3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.
• ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards 
§3 DER Classification
DER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with
IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.
Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.
Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility
interconnection practice.

"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.

import csv
import html

# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")
    try:
        v = float(x)
    except ValueError:
        return {x}
    out = {x, f"{v:g}"}
    if v == int(v):
        out.add(str(int(v)))
    return out


def read_register(path):
    if path.lower().endswith((".xlsx", ".xlsm")):
        try:
            import openpyxl
        except ImportError:
            sys.exit("--register on .xlsx needs openpyxl; export the sheet to CSV")
        wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True, read_only=True)
        rows = []
        for ws in wb.worksheets:
            rows += [["" if c is None else str(c) for c in r] for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]

DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1.
The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2.
Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3.
Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4.
Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.

5.
The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:
•
the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;
•
for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;

•
for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;
•
the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;
•
correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.

current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards

§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
•
a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
•
b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
•
c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
•
d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.
§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
•
a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
•
b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
•
c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
•
d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
•
e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).

point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.

§4   COMMUNICATIONS
§4.1   Communications transport
The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
SCADA/EMS Engineering:
•
a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or
•
b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or
•
c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
by Alleniom.
Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.
§4.2   SCADA protocol
The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§4.3   Availability
The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4   Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
record.
§5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
§5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
DIS-01 §3.4.
Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:
•
a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;

•
b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh
cadence required by §6; and
•
c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged
bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is
issued.
Compliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is
requested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be

ALLENIOM UTILITIES
DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
(612) 555-0100  ·  der.program@alleniom.com  ·  alleniom.com
July 14, 2025
Ms. Imogen Strathe
Project Manager
Halbray Community Solar LP
6120 Halbray Road
Kelloway Township, Alleron 07KT
Re:  Pre-PTO backfeed request — Halbray Field Solar Site 3 (PXA-2024-0002), feeder ALN-159 — requested date July 29, 2025
Dear Ms. Strathe:
We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025. The gating item is final electrical approval from Kelloway Township. Permit EP-25-0418 states that no permitted work shall be energized before final approval; the final inspection is booked for July 24, 2025, and no final approval is in the record yet. July 29 remains achievable if the Township passes the inspection, issues written final approval before the switching order is released, and the items below are closed. If those conditions are not met, we cannot energize on July 29 and will re-date the request with Distribution Operations.
Basis for this answer
The executed ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3 (11/18/2024) permits pre-PTO backfeed on your written request: the Company may energize the customer's facilities from the feeder for construction and commissioning power before PTO, provided the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel, with Distribution Operations switching under its own order. Your July 9, 2025 letter is that written request, and it confirms the inverters will remain disabled.
The controlling limit here is the permit, not the ISA. Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 (issued 05/12/2025) adopts the 2023 NEC and states: “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval.” The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The backfeed energizes the ac collection system and T-1 up to the open AD-1 to AD-4; the inverter skids and their ac output cables are isolated and are not energized. The collection system, transformer and 13.2 kV interconnection are permitted work, so the permit still gates the backfeed. Your letter and our commissioning checklist record the final inspection as booked for July 24, 2025; the permit itself records only that it is booked by the permit holder, and no final approval has been issued.
The ISA capacity is 2.3 MW ac (2,300 kW), matching the four 575 kW skids and the permit scope; the request does not change the executed capacity or point of interconnection. The transformer, switchboard and grounding ratings check out on the record: T-1 is 2,500 kVA, 13.2 kV to 800Y/462 V, 5.75%, giving 1,804 A secondary full-load current and 31.4 kA at CSB-1 against 65 kA switchgear; the 150E primary fuses are at 137% of the 109 A primary full-load current (NEC 450.3(A) limit 300%); the 2,000 A secondary main is at 111% of 1,804 A (limit 125%); the highest-voltage-drop collection feeder, C-4, is 1.49%; and the measured ground resistance is 3.1 ohms. The record does not yet contain the 13.2 kV interconnection conductor data or the 800 V feeder ampacity/termination basis, and it records an undersized equipment grounding conductor on the collection feeders; those items are listed below.
What is already in order for the backfeed
Halbray reports construction complete 07/03/2025; equipment schedules E-201 and E-301 Rev B (06/20/2025) record the four 575 kW skids, the 800 V collection system, CSB-1, T-1 and the 13.2 kV primary switch.
The utility RTU end-to-end point-to-point test was accepted on 07/02/2025 (TCS-02 §3.6). The POI recloser settings and protection coordination study were issued on 06/16/2025, and site acceptance items 1 to 7 were accepted in writing on 07/07/2025 (DPS-07 §5.1 and §6.2); those items are owned by Distribution Protection Engineering and are not reviewed here.
Revenue meter RM-0002 was set 07/08/2025; its test/seal confirmation is item 5 below and no test/seal record is in the file.
What must be closed before July 29, 2025
Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. (the permit holder). Confirm the 07/24/2025 booking with the Township now, pass the final inspection, and send the written final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office when issued and before the switching order is released. The permit does not require approval by 07/24/2025 itself; if approval issues after the inspection but before the switching order is released, July 29 can still hold. If the inspection is postponed or fails, or written approval is not in hand before the switching order is released, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
Collection-feeder equipment grounding conductor — Tamsworth. The equipment schedule records 1 AWG Cu in each duct for feeders C-1 to C-4, each protected by a 600 A breaker in CSB-1. NEC 2023 Table 250.122 requires 2/0 AWG Cu for a 600 A circuit, and NEC 250.122(F) requires that full-size conductor in each parallel raceway. 1 AWG is two standard sizes below the requirement. Replace or upsize the EGC in each duct to 2/0 AWG Cu (or provide a code-compliant design) and send the revised schedule and the inspection record before the 07/24/2025 final inspection. This is a code non-conformance in work the backfeed will energize.
Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send the isolation procedure and signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed. Without that confirmation, we will not release the switching order.
Construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection — Tamsworth. These need to be in the record so they do not become a second gate at the final inspection:
(a)  CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. The general warning is required by NEC 2023 110.16(A), and the label content (arc-flash boundary plus incident energy at the working distance or PPE category) is specified by NFPA 70E 130.5(H). NEC 2023 110.16(B) applies to equipment rated 600 V or less and does not apply to CSB-1 at 800 V. Confirm the installed label carries the boundary and incident energy/PPE category, or replace it.
(b)  Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method.
(c)  13.2 kV interconnection conductors. The record does not contain the 13.2 kV conductor size, insulation, ampacity, shielding/grounding and test results between PSW-1 and the point of interconnection. Provide that record, or confirm in writing that this run is utility-owned and covered by the utility work order, before the final inspection.
(d)  800 V feeder ampacity and terminations. The record gives two sets of 3 x 1/C 350 kcmil Cu per feeder and a 600 A breaker but no ampacity calculation, installation conditions or termination rating. At 75 °C two sets give 620 A against the 600 A breaker, a margin of only 3.3%; a correction factor below 0.968 would leave the pair below the breaker rating. Provide the ampacity calculation and termination basis before the final inspection.
Revenue meter test and seal — Alleniom Metering (utility action). Confirm the RM-0002 test and seal before switching; no test/seal record is in the file.
Path to July 29, 2025
If all items above, including the written final approval and the isolation confirmation, are received before the switching order is released, Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control switching. If any item slips, we will give you the next available date.
Scope of this letter
This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed and is not a permission to operate. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings, coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue position, and the system impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not reviewed here. For PTO, the installed inverters NG-XT-225 (eight) and NG-XT-125 (four) are in the body of CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025), and the witness test and SOC live-telemetry confirmation are PTO conditions; they do not stand in the way of the July 29 backfeed.
Please send the final approval, the EGC correction record and the isolation confirmation to the DER Program Office at der.program@alleniom.com. If you want to discuss the inspection date, call (612) 555-0100.
Sincerely,
S. Rennick
Commissioning, DER Program Office
Alleniom Utilities
der.program@alleniom.com  ·  (612) 555-0100

ALLENIOM UTILITIES
DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
(612) 555-0100  ·  der.program@alleniom.com  ·  alleniom.com
