Ms. Imogen Strathe
Project Manager
Halbray Community Solar LP
6120 Halbray Road
Kelloway Township, Alleron 07KT
Re:  Pre-PTO backfeed request — Halbray Field Solar Site 3 (PXA-2024-0002), feeder ALN-159 — requested date July 29, 2025
Dear Ms. Strathe:
We cannot confirm July 29, 2025 on the record as it stands at July 14, 2025. The gating item is final electrical approval from Kelloway Township. Permit EP-25-0418 states that no permitted work shall be energized before final approval; the final inspection is booked for July 24, 2025, and no final approval is in the record yet. July 29 remains achievable if the Township passes the inspection, issues written final approval before the switching order is released, and the items below are closed. If those conditions are not met, we cannot energize on July 29 and will re-date the request with Distribution Operations.
Basis for this answer
The executed ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3 (11/18/2024) permits pre-PTO backfeed on your written request: the Company may energize the customer's facilities from the feeder for construction and commissioning power before PTO, provided the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel, with Distribution Operations switching under its own order. Your July 9, 2025 letter is that written request, and it confirms the inverters will remain disabled.
The controlling limit here is the permit, not the ISA. Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 (issued 05/12/2025) adopts the 2023 NEC and states: “No permitted work shall be energized before final approval.” The permitted work includes the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and the 13.2 kV interconnection. The backfeed energizes the 13.2 kV interconnection, T-1, CSB-1 and the ac collection system up to the open AD-1 to AD-4; the inverter skids and their ac output cables are isolated and are not energized. The collection system, transformer and 13.2 kV interconnection are permitted work, so the permit still gates the backfeed. Your letter and our commissioning checklist record the final inspection as booked for July 24, 2025; the permit itself records only that it is booked by the permit holder, and no final approval has been issued.
The ISA capacity is 2.3 MW ac (2,300 kW), matching the four 575 kW skids and the permit scope; the request does not change the executed capacity or point of interconnection. The transformer, switchboard and grounding ratings check out on the record: T-1 is 2,500 kVA, 13.2 kV to 800Y/462 V, 5.75%, giving 1,804 A secondary full-load current and 31.4 kA at CSB-1 against 65 kA switchgear; the 150E primary fuses are at 137% of the 109 A primary full-load current (NEC 450.3(A) limit 300%); the 2,000 A secondary main is at 111% of 1,804 A (limit 125%); the highest-voltage-drop collection feeder, C-4, is 1.49%; and the measured ground resistance is 3.1 ohms. No rating exception was found in the equipment ratings that are recorded. The record does not yet contain the 13.2 kV interconnection conductor data or the 800 V feeder ampacity/termination basis; those are listed below as record confirmations, not as known defects.
What is already in order for the backfeed
Halbray reports construction complete 07/03/2025; equipment schedules E-201 and E-301 Rev B (06/20/2025) record the four 575 kW skids, the 800 V collection system, CSB-1, T-1 and the 13.2 kV primary switch.
The utility RTU end-to-end point-to-point test was accepted on 07/02/2025 (TCS-02 §3.6), and the POI recloser settings and protection coordination study were issued on 06/16/2025, with site acceptance items 1 to 7 accepted in writing on 07/07/2025 (DPS-07 §5.1 and §6.2). The RTU acceptance is with SCADA/EMS Engineering; the POI settings and site acceptance are with Distribution Protection Engineering; neither is reviewed here.
Revenue meter RM-0002 was set 07/08/2025; its test/seal confirmation is the final item below and no test/seal record is in the file.
What must be closed before July 29, 2025
Kelloway Township final approval — Halbray and Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. (the permit holder). Confirm the 07/24/2025 booking with the Township now, pass the final inspection, and send the written final approval to Commissioning/DER Program Office when issued and before the switching order is released. The permit does not require approval by 07/24/2025 itself; if approval issues after the inspection but before the switching order is released, July 29 can still hold. If the inspection is postponed or fails, or written approval is not in hand before the switching order is released, July 29 cannot hold and we will re-date.
Inverter isolation and lockout — Halbray/Tamsworth. Before switching, open and lock AD-1 to AD-4, confirm every inverter is disabled and incapable of export, and send the isolation procedure and signed confirmation. This is the ISA condition that the generating facility stays disabled and does not operate in parallel during the backfeed. Without that confirmation, we will not release the switching order.
Construction-record confirmations before the 07/24/2025 inspection — Tamsworth. These need to be in the record so they do not become a second gate at the final inspection:
(a)  CSB-1 arc-flash label. The equipment schedule records a label giving the nominal voltage, available fault current, clearing time and date of the calculation. The general warning is required by NEC 2023 110.16(A), and the label content (arc-flash boundary plus incident energy at the working distance or PPE category) is specified by NFPA 70E 130.5(H). NEC 2023 110.16(B) applies to equipment rated 600 V or less and does not apply to CSB-1 at 800 V. Confirm the installed label carries the boundary and incident energy/PPE category, or replace it.
(b)  Inverter ac output cable. The inverter skid schedule records 2 kV Type USE-2 in rigid steel conduit on the skid frame. NEC 2023 338.10(B)(4) does not permit single-rated USE cable in above-ground conduit except for rising from underground to a terminal. Confirm the cable is dual-rated RHW-2/USE-2 and marked for the application, or replace it with a permitted wiring method.
(c)  13.2 kV interconnection conductors. The record does not contain the 13.2 kV conductor size, insulation, ampacity, shielding/grounding and test results between PSW-1 and the point of interconnection. Provide that record, or confirm in writing that this run is utility-owned and covered by the utility work order, before the final inspection.
(d)  800 V feeder ampacity and terminations. The record gives two sets of 3 x 1/C 350 kcmil Cu per feeder and a 600 A breaker but no ampacity calculation, installation conditions or termination rating. At 75 °C the two sets give 620 A, only 3.3% above the breaker rating; provide the ampacity calculation and termination basis, including any correction for soil temperature and thermal resistivity and the NEC 250.122(B) check on the 1 AWG Cu feeder EGC, before the final inspection.
Revenue meter test and seal — Alleniom Metering (utility action). Confirm the RM-0002 test and seal before switching; no test/seal record is in the file.
Path to July 29, 2025
If all items above, including the written final approval and the isolation confirmation, are received before the switching order is released, Commissioning will ask Distribution Operations to hold the July 29, 2025 switching window. Distribution Operations will issue its own switching order and control switching. If any item slips, we will give you the next available date.
Scope of this letter
This letter addresses only the pre-PTO backfeed and is not a permission to operate. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings, coordination and DER-side protection review, switching, queue position, and the system impact study are handled by their respective owners and are not reviewed here. For PTO, the installed inverters NG-XT-225 (eight) and NG-XT-125 (four) are in the body of CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025), and the witness test and SOC live-telemetry confirmation are PTO conditions; they do not stand in the way of the July 29 backfeed.
Please send the final approval, the construction-record confirmations and the isolation confirmation to the DER Program Office at der.program@alleniom.com. If you want to discuss the inspection date, call (612) 555-0100.
Sincerely,
S. Rennick
Commissioning, DER Program Office
Alleniom Utilities

steps.message:
All requested deliverables are present, complete and validated.

## Deliverables

- **Word letter:** `/filesystem/Halbray_Backfeed_Reply.docx` — valid Microsoft Word DOCX, **2 pages**, dated **07/14/2025**, addressed to Ms. Imogen Strathe.
- **OpenProject work package:** **#47** in project 3, `DER Program Backlog Review` — “Halbray Field Solar Site 3 (PXA-2024-0002) — pre-PTO backfeed conditions,” Task, High priority, assigned to **S. Rennick**, start **2025-07-14**, due **2025-07-29**.
- **Working files:** `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv` (54 requirements), `rejected.csv`, `checklist.md`, `asks.md`, `check_halbray.py`, and `independent_review.md` with the review disposition appended.

## Determination in the letter

**07/29/2025 is not confirmed on the 07/14/2025 record.** Kelloway Township final approval under permit EP-25-0418 is the gating item; final inspection is booked for 07/24/2025 and no final approval is in the record.

The letter states that 07/29 remains achievable if written final approval issues before the switching order is released — approval need not issue by 07/24 — and these items are closed:

1. Kelloway final approval — Halbray/Tamsworth, before the switching order.
2. Inverter isolation/lockout at AD-1 to AD-4 — Halbray/Tamsworth.
3. CSB-1 arc-flash label content — Tamsworth, before the 07/24 inspection.
4. Inverter ac Type USE-2 above-ground cable — Tamsworth.
5. 13.2 kV interconnection conductor record — Tamsworth, or written confirmation it is utility-owned.
6. 800 V feeder ampacity/termination basis, including the NEC 250.122(B) EGC check — Tamsworth.
7. Revenue meter RM-0002 test/seal — Alleniom Metering, before switching.

The letter records that the backfeed energizes the 13.2 kV interconnection, T-1, CSB-1 and the collection system only up to the open AD-1 to AD-4; the inverter skids remain isolated. RTU/POI recloser acceptance, settings/coordination, switching, queue position and the SIS are expressly outside the letter; CEL, witness test and SOC telemetry are PTO items.

## Review disposition

- **Confirmed and fixed:** findings 2–10 and 12 — removed the incorrect 07/24 final-approval deadline; added the 13.2 kV and 800 V ampacity record confirmations; corrected the energized scope; corrected the arc-flash citation to NEC 110.16(A) and NFPA 70E 130.5(H); included all items in the path; tracked the meter test/seal; attributed construction-complete to Halbray; used the shared program contact; and moved the CEL statement to PTO.
- **Rejected finding 1:** NEC 2023 Table 250.122 assigns **1 AWG Cu to 600 A**; **2/0 Cu is the 1000 A row**. The recorded 1 AWG feeder EGC is at the table minimum, not undersized. The letter instead requires the NEC 250.122(B) proportionality check in the feeder ampacity basis.
- **Rejected finding 11:** REQ-PER-01 to 04 already cite `R0108` and EQ-DC cites `R0154`; the remaining blanks are table/drawing requirements with no scanner candidate.

## Validation

- `ahpele_check.py`: **no problems**.
- `ahpele_reqscan.py --check`: **68/68** strong project-document candidates reviewed, **0 unreviewed**.
- `ahpele_reqscan.py --register requirements.csv`: **54 rows**, `notfound=0`, `unmatched=0`, `multi=0`.
- `check_halbray.py`: **PASS**; worst hard-limit utilisation **1.000** on the EGC at the NEC Table 250.122 minimum, with the 250.122(B) check required in the ampacity calculation.
- DOCX renders to **2 pages**; OpenProject WP #47 read back with the correct project, subject, assignee, dates and description.
